paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by language models across three domains—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—before and after instruction tuning, as part of an evaluation of bias mitigation strategies. The vertical axis represents the bias percentage, ranging from 0 to 70, while the horizontal axis categorizes the domains. For each domain, two stacked bars are shown: a lighter shaded bar representing the bias percentage before instruction tuning, and a darker shaded bar representing the bias percentage after tuning. In the Sports domain, the bias percentage decreases from 45.42% (light gray, "No Contact Before") to 7.45% (gray with diagonal lines, "No Contact After"), and from 43.65% (light red, "Positive Contact Before") to 8.31% (red with diagonal lines, "Positive Contact After"), with a significant drop from 50.05% (light blue, "Negative Contact Before") to 8.33% (blue with diagonal lines, "Negative Contact After"). In the Community domain, bias percentages drop from 38.08% ("No Contact Before") to 0.00% ("No Contact After"), from 35.38% ("Positive Contact Before") to 0.01% ("Positive Contact After"), and from 40.79% ("Negative Contact Before") to 0.00% ("Negative Contact After"). Similarly, in the Healthcare domain, bias decreases from 40.70% ("No Contact Before") to 0.00% ("No Contact After"), from 37.51% ("Positive Contact Before") to 0.01% ("Positive Contact After"), and from 46.73% ("Negative Contact Before") to 0.11% ("Negative Contact After"). The darker bars, representing post-tuning bias, are nearly negligible in most cases, visually confirming that instruction tuning effectively reduces biases to near-zero levels across all domains, particularly in Community and Healthcare, when trained on education and workplace scenario prompts. The legend indicates that the lighter shades represent the pre-tuning state, while the darker shades represent the post-tuning state, with the darker bars stacked on top of the lighter ones, reflecting the reduction in bias. The caption emphasizes that the absence of dark bars in Community and Healthcare indicates a near-elimination of bias after tuning, supporting the conclusion that instruction tuning is effective in mitigating social biases in LLMs.
